newsitem.title: USA: O.J. Simpson rows with victim's father.
newsitem.headline: O.J. Simpson rows with victim's father.

text.p: A tension-filled day in O.J. Simpson's civil trial on Thursday ended in a shouting match between the former celebrity athlete and Fred Goldman, the father of murder victim Ron Goldman, who was killed along with Simpson's ex-wife.

The brief but loud argument occurred as Simpson was leaving the courtroom after a day that featured gruesome photographs of the two victims who were killed by a knife-wielding assailant on June 12, 1994.

Simpson was found not guilty of the murders by a criminal court jury last October but is fighting a wrongful death suit by the families of the victims, who are seeking compensatory damages for the loss of loved ones.
"Don't give me that ... dirty look," Goldman yelled at Simpson, who was standing about 25 feet (8 meters) away.
"I wasn't even looking at you; I was looking at your daughter; she was staring at me." Simpson replied. "Your daughter, she plays staring games," he added, referring to Kim Goldman.

At the time Goldman was still in the courtroom while Simpson was in the hallway outside. A bailiff and Simpson's sister, Shirley Baker, then escorted Simpson away as another bailiff called for the courtroom doors to be closed.
Goldman and his daughter, Kim, have been in attendance at the trial almost daily. Simpson had previously pointed out to reporters that Kim Goldman was always staring at him.

During the court session, the lead detective in the murder investigation disclosed for the first time the contents of a black leather travel bag Simpson had with him when he fled on the day he was to surrender to police to be arrested on double murder charges.

Former detective Tom Lange told jurors the bag contained a .357 calibre revolver loaded with six bullets, a "disguise kit" consisting of a false moustache and goatee beard, his passport, several credit cards, a change of underwear and three key rings.

Lange, who retired from the Los Angeles Police Department this year after nearly 29 years, said the items were recovered from a white Ford Bronco when Simpson was finally arrested after the famous slow-speed chase along Los Angeles freeways on June 17, five days after the murders.
Al Cowlings, Simpson's best friend who drove him on that day, was expected to testify later in the trial.
The civil case jury also saw a bloody glove found at the scene of the murders as well as a knit cap which was discovered lying close to the bodies.

Simpson, who gained fame as an actor and television pitchman following his football career, looked away and closed his eyes as the photographs were displayed, while Kim Goldman buried her face in her hands.

Testimony was interrupted when an alternate juror, a white man about 40 who works for a law firm, complained of heart pains and was taken to the hospital. He was later excused from jury duty, leaving seven alternates ready to join the 12-person panel in the event a regular juror has to leave.

Attorneys for the plaintiffs had indicated they intended to call Simpson to the witness stand around the middle of November. But lead defence lawyer Robert Baker told Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki on Thursday that Simpson would be unavailable from Nov. 12 to the end of the month while he fights for custody of his and Nicole Brown Simpson's two children, Sydney, 11, and Justin, 9.

Simpson voluntarily gave custody of the children to their maternal grandparents, Lou and Juditha Brown, at the time of his arrest in connection with the murder of their mother. He spent 16 months in jail before and during the criminal trial and sought to regain custody after he was found innocent.
